nodes.label: An alert is information, never an order
nodes.norm_label: an alert is information, never an order
nodes.rationale: With a bracket order the stop-loss and take-profit sit at the broker; alerts only report.

nodes.label: Broker keys never in chat
nodes.rationale: Keys live in env vars or Claude Desktop config.

nodes.label: "Needs approval" tool permission
nodes.rationale: Order tools are never Always allow so Claude's Allow once / Deny card always appears.

nodes.label: Paper trading by default
nodes.rationale: Going live is the user's own decision in their own config.

nodes.label: Three-gate order approval
nodes.rationale: Two yeses from the user and one PASS from the rules; strictest skill because it is the only one that can lead to a real order.

nodes.label: Four sizing limits (max loss, position cap, max order, cash)
nodes.norm_label: four sizing limits (max loss, position cap, max order, cash)
nodes.rationale: The stop decides the size; a stop too far for the max loss is refused rather than shrunk to a smaller order.

nodes.label: Fresh price rule (under 15 minutes, higher price only)
nodes.norm_label: fresh price rule (under 15 minutes, higher price only)
nodes.rationale: A price that ran up since the plan means a bigger loss at the same stop; a lower price never shrinks risk.

nodes.label: Whole shares only
nodes.rationale: Alpaca takes no fractions in a bracket order.

nodes.label: Verdict Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: trader-broker matches each order to its verdict by fingerprint so an edited order must pass again and yesterday's verdict does not count today.

nodes.label: Entry window (no entries before 9:45 or after 15:30)
nodes.norm_label: entry window (no entries before 9:45 or after 15:30)

nodes.label: Stop rules (or-mid, or-low, price, pct, atr)
nodes.norm_label: stop rules (or-mid, or-low, price, pct, atr)

nodes.label: Closed-bar trigger
nodes.rationale: A wick above is not an entry; only a completed bar that CLOSES above the level counts, and never call an entry early.

nodes.label: Plan refusals (stop at/above entry, too tight for spread)
nodes.norm_label: plan refusals (stop at/above entry, too tight for spread)
nodes.rationale: A risk under 0.05% of price would be stopped out by normal wiggle; never loosen anything on its own.

nodes.label: Stop rounding away from entry
nodes.rationale: Stop rounds down to the cent for a long; target rounds half up.

nodes.label: Opening-Range Breakout Scan
nodes.rationale: Two stages: cheap spark closes as a necessary condition so no breakout is lost, then v8 charts with real highs/lows capped by --max-confirm.

nodes.label: Starter Config ($5,000 budget, $50 max loss, paper)
nodes.norm_label: starter config ($5,000 budget, $50 max loss, paper)

nodes.label: Entries vs Exits (exits never blocked)
nodes.rationale: Getting out must always be possible, so exits are checked only for format, asset and short sales; other rules become warnings.

nodes.label: Higher of Plan Entry and Fresh Price
nodes.norm_label: higher of plan entry and fresh price
nodes.rationale: A plan written at 10:15 cannot understate the risk at 10:55 after the price ran up.

nodes.label: PDT Guard
nodes.rationale: FINRA removed the $25,000 PDT minimum (Regulatory Notice 26-10) but some brokers still apply it, so the guard is optional.

nodes.label: Three-Gate Order Approval (risk PASS + typed yes + Allow once)
nodes.norm_label: three-gate order approval (risk pass + typed yes + allow once)

nodes.norm_label: fx sessions (sydney, tokyo, london, new york)

nodes.norm_label: jarvis env settings (jarvis_offline, jarvis_model, jarvis_effort, jarvis_tool_timeout)

nodes.label: JARVIS Trading Assistant
nodes.rationale: Claude picks the skill, runs it and summarises; JARVIS never places, approves or records orders, it only shows tickets.

nodes.label: One-off flag (net income above operating income)
nodes.norm_label: one-off flag (net income above operating income)

nodes.label: Compare like with like (year-over-year growth)
nodes.rationale: Many businesses are seasonal, so growth is measured against the same quarter a year earlier.

nodes.label: Derived Q4 (10-K minus three quarters)
nodes.rationale: Companies do not file a Q4 10-Q.

nodes.label: Earnings gap risk
nodes.rationale: A stop does not protect against a gap; the stock can open past it, so flag a report inside the trade.

nodes.label: SEC User-Agent requirement
nodes.rationale: Tool refuses to call SEC without a real name/email User-Agent and stays under 10 requests/second.

nodes.label: A stop is a plan, not a guarantee
nodes.norm_label: a stop is a plan, not a guarantee
nodes.rationale: A gap or fast market can fill past it.

nodes.label: Flat by time (15:55, no overnight hold)
nodes.norm_label: flat by time (15:55, no overnight hold)

nodes.label: FX sessions (Sydney, Tokyo, London, New York, overlap)
nodes.norm_label: fx sessions (sydney, tokyo, london, new york, overlap)

nodes.label: Alert rule types (above/below/stop/target/pct_move/time/opening_bell)
nodes.rationale: Each alert rings once (state file) so the user is not spammed; plan rules carry the plan's date so yesterday's stop never rings today.

nodes.label: Flat by close alert
nodes.rationale: before_close time rules move 3 hours earlier on 1:00 p.m. early closes.

nodes.label: History: Same Rule on Past Sessions
nodes.norm_label: history: same rule on past sessions

nodes.label: Break-Even Verdict (1 in 1+R)
nodes.rationale: A bigger target needs to win less often to break even, so verdict weighs target R rather than target-first vs stop-first alone.

nodes.label: Full-Session 5-Minute Bar Pool
nodes.rationale: Only full 78-bar sessions before the plan date; 1-min bars cover only ~7 days, too few for a fair pool.

nodes.label: Seed 19 (reproducible draws)
nodes.rationale: Same plan, data and seed give same numbers on any machine; always state the seed.

nodes.label: News Tags (earnings, analyst, legal, deal, halt, regulatory, macro)
nodes.norm_label: news tags (earnings, analyst, legal, deal, halt, regulatory, macro)

nodes.label: Voice Mode
nodes.rationale: Orders are never confirmed by voice: /fxsend always needs a typed yes.

nodes.label: FX scan (trend, 20-day breakout, RSI, ATR in pips)
nodes.norm_label: fx scan (trend, 20-day breakout, rsi, atr in pips)

nodes.label: Honest limits (indicative delayed mids, no spread/swap/slippage)
nodes.norm_label: honest limits (indicative delayed mids, no spread/swap/slippage)

nodes.label: Lot sizing from risk percent with leverage cap
nodes.norm_label: lot sizing from risk percent with leverage cap

nodes.label: Pip math (JPY pairs, pip value per lot)
nodes.norm_label: pip math (jpy pairs, pip value per lot)

nodes.label: FX send gate (risk check + explicit yes + ALLOW_LIVE)
nodes.norm_label: fx send gate (risk check + explicit yes + allow_live)
nodes.rationale: Real accounts require MT5_ALLOW_LIVE=1 / OANDA_ALLOW_LIVE=1 in addition to an explicit typed yes.

nodes.label: trader-pelosi (Pelosi Tracker)
nodes.rationale: It is fast, not early: PTRs are due up to 45 days after the trade, so there is no inside information, only public filings read quickly.

nodes.label: Headlines Are Leads, Not Facts
nodes.rationale: Open and read the story or filing before reporting; filings beat headlines because an 8-K is what the company told the SEC.

nodes.label: 45-Day Disclosure Delay
nodes.rationale: Each row shows days between trade and filing; over 45 flagged late.

nodes.label: Quote the Filing, Not a Tracker
nodes.norm_label: quote the filing, not a tracker
nodes.rationale: Third-party trackers can be off (Capitol Trades showed Pelosi trade dates one day early); the PTR wins.

nodes.label: Senate eFD Manual Route
nodes.rationale: The Senate site requires a user-accepted legal agreement, so the skill never clicks or automates it.
